items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: we're sitting here with your friend and your bass player, Smitty.

ctx.x: What's the way it was. I just want to say we're sitting here with your friend and your bass player, Smitty. He's sitting here with us. He's from New Orleans, too, so he understands this whole thing... [ETC.] So what did you tell us about David Jones?

So David Jones was a fantastic musician. David Jones was a showman. He played mellophone also. Everybody respected David Jones. And he played this mellophone, so all trumpet players looked at him with respect, and all saxophone players, none of them had the nerve to even challenge him, not at that time, in 1930. But he never claimed nothin' or never thought about nothin'. He was more of a teacher. Everybody in this town, you'd say David Jones... David Jones was like, when I was in New York, Benny Carter.
